children: CEO John Whelan said the company supports a united Canada, as the Alberta province prepares to vote on whether to begin the constitutional process toward a binding independence referendum, Bloomberg reported Tuesday.
"Canada and Alberta work best when people, products, energy, and investment can move freely and reliably across the country," Whelan said, making Imperial Oil
the first major energy company in the province to stake a firm position on the movement to break away from Canada.

A recent study commissioned by the Alberta government was released showing that any secession process could reduce gross domestic product by at least 2.2% in the first five years in a good scenario, or more than 10% in a poor one.

Whelan also said he shares Alberta Premier Danielle Smith's goal of doubling oil production in the province and lauded moves the Alberta and Canadian governments have made to encourage production growth.

"With a supportive fiscal and regulatory framework, Imperial has the potential to double our gross operated upstream production while also advancing additional downstream biofuel production," the CEO said.

title: Imperial Oil CEO urges Alberta to reject separatist push
